content.content:
**YPP Threshold Changes (effective February 1, 2027)**

- **Long-form:** New applicants need **8,000 watch hours over 365 days**, up from 4,000 hours of public watch time in a year.
- **Shorts:** New applicants need **20 million Shorts views over 90 days**, up from 10 million.
- **Subscribers:** The article doesn't say whether the 1,000-subscriber requirement changes.
- **Shorts ads:** Regardless of how a creator qualifies, they need at least **10 million Shorts views over 90 days** to earn from Shorts ads. Partners who drop below that level have their Shorts ads paused, and they're restored automatically when they return above it.

**Grandfathering**

Creators already in the Partner Program keep their status and don't have to meet the new thresholds. The Shorts ad cutoff, however, applies to everyone.

**Fan Funding**

The Fan Funding requirements are unchanged: 500 subscribers, at least three qualified uploads in the past 90 days, and either 3,000 yearly long-form watch hours or 3 million Shorts views over 90 days.

**YouTube's Stated Reasons**

- **Ecosystem growth:** YouTube VP of Creator Product Amjad Hanif described the changes as "adjustments based on the amazing growth of the creator ecosystem over the past few years."
- **Meaningful Shorts revenue:** Hanif said YouTube wants Shorts ads to be a "meaningful" revenue stream, and the article notes that generating significant Shorts earnings takes millions of views.
- **Shifting to other revenue:** YouTube says it is adding incentive programs, such as Shopping bonuses, brand deal incentives, and boosts for starting or growing trends, for channels below the 10 million view threshold. The company says it will share more details later.
- **Creator economy trends:** The article notes that creators increasingly earn from direct fan funding, and that the update preserves ad revenue for existing Partners.

content.content:
**When disclosure is required**

Creators must disclose realistic GenAI content that alters real events or places, makes a real person appear to say or do something they didn't, or creates music that's the main focus of a video. Examples include:
- "AI generated extra footage of a real place, like a video of a surfer in Maui"
- "Making it look like a real person has been arrested or imprisoned"

**When disclosure isn't required**

- **Clearly unrealistic content:** Fantasy scenes, such as "Someone riding a unicorn through a fantastical world," don't need disclosure.
- **Animation:** A fully animated video with an AI-generated missile, for example, doesn't need disclosure.
- **Script and production help:** Using generative AI for "a video outline, script, thumbnail, title" is listed as minor and doesn't need disclosure.
- **Voice:** Cloning your own voice for voiceovers or dubs is listed as minor. The page doesn't specifically address AI voices generated for other people, so realistic-content rules would be the main guide there.
- **Minor edits:** Beauty filters, color adjustments, and audio repair don't need disclosure.

**Consequences of not disclosing**

Creators who consistently don't disclose may face a manual label, or penalties such as content removal or suspension from the YouTube Partner Program. The page also notes that "Disclosing AI content alone won't limit a video's audience" and that Community Guidelines apply to AI content too.

The page doesn't have a section titled "Inauthentic content." The policy appears as **"Generic or Repetitive Content"**, and a July 15, 2025 update says it was renamed "inauthentic content." The page also doesn't divide policies into three categories. Each policy has an "allowed" subsection and a "violation" subsection.

**Generic or Repetitive (Inauthentic) Content**

- **Definition:** "Generic or repetitive content includes content that looks like it's made with a template." It may also feel repetitive after viewers watch several videos from the same channel.
- **Allowed:** Videos with the same intro and outro if the main content differs. Series or review channels where each video has a distinct storyline, focus, or concept.
- **Not allowed:**
  - Repetitive content with low educational value or minimal variation.
  - Characters repeatedly placed in the same situation with the same outcome.
  - Image slideshows, templated storylines, or scrolling text with little narrative or value.
  - AI-generated content from "generic or unoriginal templates" that lacks the creator's original perspective.
- **Reviewers may check:** the main theme, most-viewed and newest videos, the biggest share of watch time, metadata (titles, thumbnails, descriptions), and the "About" section.

**Reused Content**

- **Definition:** Channels that repurpose content already online without significant original commentary, substantive changes, or educational or entertainment value. The page also calls this "duplicative or scraped" content.
- **Allowed:** Critical reviews using clips, rewritten dialogue or voiceovers, sports replays that explain plays, reaction videos with commentary, edited footage with a storyline and commentary, Shorts remixes with added original content, content that features the uploader, and substantially edited footage.
- **Not allowed:**
  - Movie clips edited together with little narrative.
  - Compilations from other social media sites.
  - Song collections, even with permission.
  - Content uploaded many times by other creators.
  - Promotion of others' content.
  - Downloaded content without substantive changes.
  - Reactions with no voice commentary.
  - Readings of others' material, such as website or news text.
  - Songs altered only in pitch or speed.
- **Reviewers may check:** the channel's videos, channel description, video titles, and video descriptions. The policy applies to the whole channel.

**Not covered on this page:** The text doesn't specifically address text-to-speech or story channels. It mentions AI in the policies above and in the "Unsatisfying or Off-putting Content" section, which allows AI for tasks like editing scripts or generating a background visual. It also has a separate "AI Personas Related to Sensitive Topics" policy.

**How Shorts ad revenue sharing works**

Only monetizing partners who have accepted the Shorts Monetization Module can earn from Shorts ads. Creators also need at least 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days to be eligible for a given month.

**The four steps**

1. **Pool revenue:** Each month, ad revenue from the Shorts Feed is combined. The article says it's "used to both reward creators and help cover costs of music licensing."
2. **Calculate the Creator Pool:** Revenue is allocated based on engaged views and music use. Shorts without music send all their associated revenue to the Creator Pool.
3. **Allocate the Creator Pool:** Each creator receives a share based on their portion of total engaged views in each country.
4. **Apply the revenue share:** Creators keep 45% of their allocated revenue. The article states: "Monetizing creators will keep 45% of their allocated revenue, regardless if music was used or not."

**Music deduction**

If a Short contains music, the revenue from its views is split between the Creator Pool and music partners, based on the number of tracks. With one track, half goes to the Creator Pool. With two tracks, one third does. The music deduction affects only the pool split, not your individual allocation. Per the article, a creator's allocation "is not affected by your use of a music track."

**Example (from the article)**

- $100,000 ad revenue in Country A, with 20% of Shorts using one track
- Creator Pool: $90,000, with $10,000 going to music licensing
- A creator with 1% of engaged views receives $900 from the pool
- At 45%, the creator earns $405

**Ineligible views**

YouTube doesn't count engaged views that fall into these categories:
- Non-original Shorts, such as "unedited clips from others' movies or TV shows"
- Artificial or fake views, such as those from "automated click or scroll bots"
- Views of Shorts that conflict with the advertiser-friendly content guidelines

**Dates**
- **Announced:** August 10, 2026
- **Terms acceptance deadline:** January 31, 2027 (a Sunday)
- **New thresholds and activity rules take effect:** February 1, 2027

**Entry thresholds (new applicants)**
- **Subscribers:** 1,000, unchanged.
- **Long-form path:** 8,000 qualified watch hours in the last 365 days, up from 4,000.
- **Shorts path:** 20 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days, up from 10 million.
- The two paths don't cross-count. A channel must meet one threshold on its own.

**Grandfathering**
- Channels already in YPP keep their status and ad and Premium earnings. The article quotes YouTube saying the new entry rules "will only apply to new applicants."
- The article notes no stated sunset and no re-qualification requirement.

**Deadline to apply under the old thresholds**
- The article doesn't state an application cutoff. It only says the higher bar applies to applicants not yet admitted from February 1, 2027.

**Shorts 10M-view rule**
- The article mentions a "separate 10 million-view monthly requirement for Shorts Creator Pool payouts," but only in passing, in the creator reaction section. It gives no further detail.

**Activity rules (from February 1, 2027)**
- Any one of: 1,000 qualified watch hours in 365 days, 1 million qualified Shorts views in 90 days, or 2 long-form videos or 5 Shorts uploaded every 90 days.
- Channels below these get a 90-day window to meet the watch-hour or view condition.

**Fan funding and other expanded YPP features (unchanged)**
- Super Chat, channel memberships, YouTube Creator Partnerships, and YouTube Shopping stay at 500 subscribers plus either 3,000 qualified watch hours (365 days) or 3 million qualified Shorts views (90 days).

**Terms acceptance**
- Creators must accept the Watch Page Monetization, Shorts Monetization, and, where applicable, Commerce Product modules in YouTube Studio by January 31, 2027. Missing it stops earnings from those features on February 1, 2027, but acceptance can be made later to restore access and doesn't affect YPP status.
- MCN-owned channels are accepted by the network. Affiliate channels must accept individually.

**Incentive programs**
- The article says incentive programs were promised alongside the change, but it doesn't describe them. It notes none has published criteria yet.

**Official sources cited**
- Community post, "Updates to the YouTube Partner Program - New earning opportunities & changes to eligibility," by Jensen from Team YouTube: support.google.com/youtube/thread/451804019
- Help Center article, "Changes to the YouTube Partner Program." The article names it but doesn't link to it.

**Key points for creators outside the U.S.**

- **Withholding rates:** Rates run from 0% to 30%, depending on whether your country has a treaty with the U.S. The page states, "tax withholding rates are between 0-30% on earnings you get from U.S. viewers."

- **Which earnings are taxed:** Only U.S. viewer revenue is subject to withholding, and only if you submit valid tax info. The page says, "Only the portion of your earnings from viewers in the United States will be subject to tax withholding."

- **Default if no tax info is submitted:** Withholding can reach the maximum rate. For individuals, the page says backup withholding applies to total worldwide earnings. For non-U.S. business accounts, the default is 30% of U.S. earnings. The deadline is Dec. 10: "If tax info isn't provided by Dec. 10th, Google may be required to deduct up to 24% of your total earnings worldwide."

- **Treaty benefits:** A treaty can lower the rate for certain income types, such as Other Copyright Royalties (including YPP) and Services (including AdSense). The page's example shows a creator in India whose rate drops to 15% under the U.S.–India treaty. The page advises confirming eligibility with a tax advisor.

- **W-8BEN:** The page doesn't name this form. It refers only to an "updated W-8 tax form" in the refund section.

- **Colombia:** The page doesn't mention Colombia or any treaty with it. India is the only country cited, as an example.

content.content:
**Determining if content is "made for kids"**

YouTube says creators should weigh several factors, including the subject matter, whether children are the intended audience (for example, as shown in metadata), and whether the video has child actors or models. Other factors include characters, toys, or celebrities that appeal to children, simple songs or games, and whether the content is advertised to children. The page notes that having some of these factors doesn't automatically make content made for kids. One example of made for kids content is when "Children are the primary audience of the video."

**General audience vs. made for kids**

Content isn't made for kids just because it's family friendly, covers an activity associated with children, or might be seen by kids. Examples of general audience content include a DIY video about remaking dolls, a family vlog about an amusement park visit, and a gaming video with adult humor. Mixed audience content, which targets children as one of several audiences, counts as made for kids.

**Animated characters and gaming content**

Animated characters or cartoon figures that appeal to children are a factor toward made for kids. However, animated content that appeals to everyone is listed as general audience. For gaming, the page lists games as a factor, but a gaming video with adult humor is general audience.

**Consequences**

The page doesn't list which features are disabled for made for kids content. It says videos set as made for kids are more likely to be recommended alongside other kids' videos. It also warns that "Failure to set your content appropriately may result in consequences on YouTube" and may have legal consequences under COPPA and other laws. It adds that YouTube's systems may not identify content the FTC considers made for kids, so creators are responsible for setting it correctly.

content.content:
**Features restricted on made for kids content**

For videos and live streams, the article says "the following features won't be available on individual videos or live streams":
- "Autoplay on home"
- "Cards or end screens"
- "Video watermarks"
- "Channel Memberships"
- "Comments"
- "Donate button"
- "Likes and dislikes on YouTube Music"
- "Live chat or live chat donations"
- "Merchandise and ticketing"
- "Notification bell"
- "Personalized advertising"
- "Playback in the Miniplayer"
- "Super Chat or Super Stickers"
- "Save to playlist and Save to watch later"

If the whole channel is set as made for kids, all of the above apply, plus "Posts" and "Ask Studio." The channel also loses "Channel Memberships" and the notification bell.

The article doesn't mention Shorts-specific features.

**Audience setting options**

*Channel level* (Settings > Channel > Advanced Settings > Audience) applies to existing and future videos. The options are:
- "Yes, set this channel as made for kids. I mostly upload content that's made for kids."
- "No, set this channel as not made for kids. I almost never upload content that's made for kids."
- "I want to review this setting for every video."

If you skip the channel setting, you must identify each video yourself. Video settings override the channel setting.

*Video level* offers "Yes, it's 'Made for Kids'" or "No, it's not 'Made for Kids'" during upload or when editing existing videos.

**If YouTube overrides the setting**

YouTube uses machine learning and says it may "override your audience setting choice in cases of error or abuse." If you haven't set an audience yet, YouTube may set one for you, and you can usually change it. If you've already set it and YouTube detects error or abuse, the video may show "Set to Made for Kids," and you can't change it. You can appeal once per video in YouTube Studio. A successful appeal removes the made for kids setting, while an unsuccessful one keeps it.

The article covers three categories of "inauthentic content" that can't be monetized, but it doesn't address AI voice, faceless channels, animation, or gaming, and it gives no numbers of affected channels.

**1. Generic, repetitive, or template-based content**
- Covers material easily made with AI, CGI, or templates, with little variation between videos, which leads to near-identical uploads across a channel.
- Tutorials can fall here if they reproduce content already common on the platform instead of being original.
- Halprin describes such videos as lacking a story structure: "They're very generic and don't really have a narrative arc."

**2. "Off-putting" content**
- Content designed to be distressing or emotionally manipulative to drive views.
- Example: a video of an animal in distress that someone then rescues.
- Channels dedicated to this kind of content are removed from the YPP, whether or not the content is AI-generated.

**3. AI personas discussing sensitive topics**
- AI personas are AI-made representations of real people.
- YouTube doesn't want to encourage their use for sensitive subjects, specifically finance, legal issues, healthcare, and medical issues.

**Monetizable content:** The article gives no explicit examples. Halprin said AI can enhance creativity and that high-volume, high-quality content is what YouTube wants in the YPP.

**Channel-level enforcement:** Per Halprin, any channel with too much of any of the three content types will be unable to monetize. The clarified policies rolled out July 16 and apply to all YPP members. The article doesn't specify what "too much" means.

Official Roblox documentation and third-party guides agree on the core terms. The main points:

- **Payout:** The reward is a 35% share of a qualifying new or returning user's first $100 in Robux purchases, applied during their first 60 days. When one of these qualifying users joins or returns and is attributed to a Creator, the Creator earns a 35% revenue share on their first $100 of Qualifying Purchases anywhere on the platform during their first 60 days. Qualifying purchases are the purchase of Robux, Roblox Premium, or UGC subscriptions.
- **Who counts:** A user must be new or reactivated. Returning users must have been inactive for at least 60 days.
- **Attribution paths:** Per a third-party guide, credit can come from a Share Link, a direct link, or searching the experience's name. The Share Link path requires the user to play that experience for 10+ minutes that day. Direct-link and search paths exclude Share Link users.
- **Experience requirement:** The official docs say the experience must maintain an average of 100+ DAU for 60 days after the joining or rejoining date.
- **Creator requirements:** Developers must have an ID-verified account in good standing and a valid DevEx account. Eligibility can be checked in the Creator Dashboard.
- **Tracking:** Share Link performance is in Creator Dashboard → Analytics → Share Links.

Sources differ on some details. A DevForum launch post describes the Tipalti registration requirement, while the Roblox Wiki and a third-party guide describe ID verification and DevEx. The Roblox Wiki also says recipients must be Active Spenders, meaning they have spent at least $9.99 in the past 60 days, which applies to the Daily Engagement reward rather than Audience Expansion. The official docs are the most reliable source here. The obby.fun guide also says its earnings figures are a planning model, not a payout promise.

I ran one search. It did not return the full text of the guidelines, so the points below come from secondary sources and snippets, not a complete official document.

- **Channel names:** The official guidelines page snippet covers game titles, not channel names. It bars "Roblox," "Blox," or similar names in the titles of games published on or after June 22, 2022, and says older titles are unaffected (titles of Games containing Roblox or a name similar to Roblox that were published on the platform before such date are not affected by this prohibition). I found no snippet confirming a rule for channel names specifically.
- **Disclaimer:** A Roblox Developer Forum staff post says that if your channel or fan site uses "Roblox" or "Blox," please make sure you say that your page is not affiliated with Roblox. This is the closest match to your disclaimer question, though it is a forum post, not the guidelines text.
- **Monetized videos:** The same staff post says creators may continue monetizing that content (such as through YouTube ad revenue) when using Roblox avatars. A third-party blog says Roblox's help center allows gameplay videos with licensed music to be monetized on YouTube, but I could not verify that wording on Roblox's own page.
- **Logo and implied endorsement:** The official page says the Roblox Logo and Roblox Tilt are not permitted for general use on any creative materials or copy (unless it's part of the Official Badge). A third-party summary adds that creators must not imply an official partnership with or endorsement by Roblox.

Sources: the official Roblox help article, a Roblox Developer Forum staff post, and a third-party blog. The blog and fan wiki are secondary, and the forum post is not official guideline text. The exact guideline wording on channel names and monetization should be checked directly on Roblox's help page.

Search results point to three main themes, though the rate data is thin and mostly from marketplaces and blogs.

**Platform revenue-share dispute:** Roblox planned beta tools in April 2026 that let creators tag content as advertising. The exact revenue share percentage has not been disclosed. Creator YouTuber KreekCraft criticized the move, and developers on the forum objected that Roblox takes a share of brand deals it didn't originate. Treat this source as one side of a contested story.

**Rates:** These figures come from marketplace listings and blog posts, not audited data. One blog cites a mid-tier Roblox YouTuber with 200K–500K followers quoting $500 to $2,500 for a dedicated Roblox integration, and a smaller creator at 50K–150K might charge $150–$600. A CollabPals profile for a Roblox-niche channel lists a YouTube Short at $30 to $50, with rates based on 2026 industry CPM data by niche. Shoutout listings on CollabPals run from $1.50/shoutout for a nano creator to higher tiers.

**Market context:** One source reports that the biggest Roblox creators averaged $1.3 million in earnings in 2025. It also notes that Grow a Garden and Steal a Brainrot reached their records without significant paid influencer marketing.

**Gaps:** My search didn't cover disclosure rules for shorts or story channels, or whether the labeling tools launched on schedule. For those, a follow-up search on Roblox's advertising disclosure policy and FTC endorsement guidance would be needed.

I found no results about Royale Luna specifically, and nothing about an April 2026 remonetization. The results cover the broader context, though.

- **Background on the policy:** YouTube renamed and clarified it back in July 2025, shifting from "repetitious content" to "inauthentic content" to better catch low-effort, scaled-up videos.
- **Earlier Roblox-related wave:** In late December 2025, a moderation error hit gaming channels. A wave of Minecraft and Roblox channels lost their monetization overnight, and TeamYouTube responded shortly after, saying they're looking into it. The flagging reason appeared to be YouTube's automated systems flagging channels for "harmful content involving minors."
- **2026 enforcement:** January 2026 - YouTube launched a large-scale enforcement campaign targeting inauthentic content, removing monetization from many channels worldwide. In July 2026, YouTube reworked the guidance under its inauthentic content policy, breaking out three specific categories of video that will get creators' channels demonetized.

Nothing I found confirms the specific Royale Luna case, its cause, or any April 2026 TeamYouTube reversal. A search on her name directly, or on the channel's own statements, would be needed for that.

# Informe: canal faceless de historias animadas de Roblox en Shorts (corte: 12 de noviembre de 2026)

**Hallazgo que cambia el plan:** el 1 de febrero de 2027 YouTube duplica los umbrales de ingreso para solicitantes nuevos y exige 10 millones de vistas de Shorts cada 90 días para cobrar anuncios de Shorts. Un canal que arranca hoy casi seguro entra bajo las reglas nuevas.

Limitación de la investigación: la red local bloquea los dominios de Roblox (filtro Fortinet), así que no pude leer sus páginas oficiales. Lo de Roblox sale de fragmentos de búsqueda y fuentes secundarias, y lo marco como tal.

## 1. Programa de Socios de YouTube (YPP)

**Umbrales vigentes hoy (oficial):**
- **Nivel de financiación de fans:** 500 suscriptores, 3 videos públicos en los últimos 90 días y 3.000 horas de reproducción en 12 meses o 3 millones de vistas de Shorts en 90 días. Desbloquea membresías, Super Chat, Super Stickers, Super Thanks y Shopping. No da ingresos por anuncios.
- **Nivel completo (anuncios y Premium):** 1.000 suscriptores y 4.000 horas en 12 meses o 10 millones de vistas de Shorts en 90 días.
- Las horas de Shorts vistas en el feed no cuentan para las 4.000 horas, y las dos rutas no se combinan.
- Colombia figura en la lista de países para ambos niveles.

**Cambio desde el 1 de febrero de 2027 (anunciado el 10 de agosto de 2026):**
- Solicitantes nuevos al nivel completo: 8.000 horas en 365 días o 20 millones de vistas de Shorts en 90 días. Los 1.000 suscriptores no cambian.
- Para cobrar anuncios de Shorts, cualquier canal necesita 10 millones de vistas de Shorts en los últimos 90 días. Si baja, el reparto se pausa y se reactiva solo al volver a superarlo.
- Los canales que ya están en el YPP conservan su estado. El nivel de financiación de fans no cambia.
- Según ppc.land habrá requisitos de actividad: 1.000 horas en 365 días, 1 millón de vistas de Shorts en 90 días, o subir 2 videos largos o 5 Shorts cada 90 días.
- YouTube promete incentivos para canales por debajo de los 10 millones (bonos de Shopping, incentivos por acuerdos de marca, impulsos por tendencias), sin criterios publicados aún.
- No verificado: si basta con solicitar antes del 1 de febrero o hay que estar admitido. Según ppc.land, el umbral nuevo aplica a quien no esté admitido en esa fecha.

**Pago e impuestos desde Colombia:**
- Se paga por AdSense para YouTube, en USD. La tabla de Google para Colombia indica un límite de 6.500 USD por pago individual; lo que exceda se divide en varios pagos.
- El umbral mínimo de pago de 100 USD es el estándar conocido, pero no lo pude confirmar en la página oficial en esta sesión. Tampoco confirmé los métodos de pago disponibles para Colombia.
- Retención de EE. UU.: solo aplica a ingresos de espectadores en EE. UU., entre 0 % y 30 % según tratado. Si no envías la información fiscal, Google puede retener hasta 24 % de los ingresos mundiales.
- Colombia no tiene tratado de renta con EE. UU. (fuente secundaria: air.io), así que con el W-8BEN la retención sería 30 % sobre la parte de EE. UU. Con audiencia mayoritariamente estadounidense, es casi 30 % de todo.
- La página de Google habla de "formulario W-8" sin nombrar el W-8BEN; para persona natural es ese. Fuentes secundarias dicen que vence al final del tercer año calendario.
- No investigué la tributación colombiana (renta, IVA por exportación de servicios); consúltala con un contador.

Fuentes:
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13429240

- https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/2850006
- https://air.io/es/monetization/youtube-tax-info-w-8ben

## 2. Monetización de Shorts y RPM

**Mecánica (oficial):**
1. Se suman los ingresos de anuncios del feed de Shorts por país.
2. Se calcula el fondo de creadores: un Short sin música aporta todo su ingreso; con una pista aporta la mitad; con dos, un tercio.
3. El fondo se reparte según tu porcentaje de vistas con interacción en cada país.
4. Te quedas con el 45 % de lo asignado, uses música o no.

No cuentan los Shorts no originales, las vistas artificiales ni el contenido no apto para anunciantes. Del fondo de Premium, los Shorts también reciben 45 %.

**RPM de Shorts (USD por 1.000 vistas; todas son fuentes de terceros):**

| Audiencia | Rango | Fuente |
|---|---|---|
| EE. UU. | 0,328 (mediana de socios AIR, 274 canales) | air.io |
| EE. UU. | 0,10 a 0,32 | fluxnote |
| General, mayoría de creadores | 0,03 a 0,10 | vidIQ |
| Reino Unido, Canadá, Australia, Alemania | 0,16 a 0,19 | air.io |
| México | 0,03 a 0,04 | fluxnote (metodología débil) |
| Brasil | 0,03 a 0,05 | fluxnote (metodología débil) |
| Nicho gaming en Shorts | 0,17 | air.io |

No encontré un dato de Colombia ni testimonios de creadores individuales con cifras verificables; lo más sólido es la muestra agregada de AIR.

**Videos largos de gaming:** AIR reporta RPM entre 1,79 y 3,42 USD (el artículo es inconsistente entre ejemplos), con mediana general de unos 2.300 USD por millón de vistas. En gaming, los Shorts rinden cerca de 9,5 % del RPM de los largos. No hallé un RPM específico de Roblox.

**Estimación por 1 millón de vistas de Shorts (mía, con esos rangos):**
- **Audiencia mayoritariamente de EE. UU.:** 100 a 330 USD brutos. Tras la retención de 30 % sobre la parte estadounidense (suponiendo 70 % de vistas de EE. UU.), unos 80 a 260 USD netos.
- **Audiencia mayoritariamente LATAM:** 30 a 50 USD, casi sin retención.
- **Referencia en largos de gaming:** 1.800 a 3.400 USD por millón de vistas.

Con el piso de 10 millones de vistas cada 90 días (unos 3,3 millones al mes), un canal que apenas lo cumple ganaría unos 330 a 1.100 USD brutos al mes con audiencia de EE. UU., o 100 a 170 con audiencia LATAM.

Fuentes:
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220
- https://air.io/en/air-data-findings/youtube-shorts-rpm-vs-long-form-how-much-do-shorts-earn-in-2026
- https://fluxnote.io/guides/youtube-shorts-rpm-by-country
- https://vidiq.com/blog/post/youtube-shorts-monetization/

## 3. Políticas que pueden bloquear la monetización

**Contenido no auténtico** (renombrado desde "contenido repetitivo" el 15 de julio de 2025; aclarado el 16 de julio de 2026 en tres categorías no monetizables):
1. **Genérico o repetitivo:** contenido que parece hecho con plantilla, personajes puestos repetidamente en la misma situación con el mismo desenlace, tramas de plantilla, contenido de IA de plantillas genéricas sin perspectiva propia del creador.
2. **Insatisfactorio o desagradable:** contenido diseñado para angustiar o manipular emocionalmente.
3. **Personas de IA en temas sensibles:** finanzas, legal, salud.

Lo que sí se permite: misma intro y outro con contenido distinto, y series donde cada video tiene trama, enfoque o concepto propio. Usar IA para editar guiones o generar un fondo no descalifica por sí solo.

La evaluación es a nivel de canal: tema principal, videos más vistos y más recientes, metadatos y la sección "Acerca de". YouTube no definió cuánto es "demasiado".

**Contenido reutilizado:** no aplica a animación propia. Sí aplicaría si usas clips de otros, audios virales sin transformar o guiones leídos de Reddit u otras webs ("lecturas de material ajeno" está en la lista de lo no permitido).

**Divulgación de contenido alterado o sintético:**
- Solo es obligatoria para contenido realista que pueda confundirse con real (personas reales, eventos o lugares reales).
- No se requiere para animación, contenido claramente irreal, ni para ayuda de IA en guion, esquema, título o miniatura.
- Voz de IA: la página solo exime explícitamente clonar tu propia voz. Una voz sintética genérica sobre ficción animada no encaja en los casos obligatorios, pero no hay una exención literal; es mi interpretación. No uses voces clonadas de personas reales.
- No divulgar de forma reiterada puede llevar a etiqueta forzada, eliminación o suspensión del YPP.

**Casos reales:**
- **Diciembre de 2025:** varios canales de Minecraft y Roblox desmonetizados de un día para otro por un aparente error automático ("contenido dañino con menores"). TeamYouTube dijo que lo revisaba; no hallé el desenlace.
- **Enero de 2026:** ola de "contenido no auténtico" que golpeó sobre todo a operadores con 10 o más canales automatizados. Un canal de lore de Warhammer fue restituido tras revisión humana.
- **14 de abril de 2026:** la creadora de roleplay de Roblox Royale Luna publicó en X que la desmonetizaron por "contenido no auténtico" pese a guionar, grabar y editar todo ella misma. Solo lo vi en el fragmento de búsqueda; no confirmé el desenlace.
- No encontré un caso documentado de un canal de historias de Roblox con voz de IA aprobado en 2026.

**Qué hacer para seguir siendo monetizable (deducido de la política):**
- Dale a cada historia un arco narrativo distinto; evita la fórmula con el mismo giro.
- Usa personajes y universo recurrentes propios, con escenas construidas por ti.
- Varía títulos y miniaturas.
- Mantén un solo canal, no una red de clones.
- Guarda archivos de Studio, guiones y línea de tiempo como evidencia para una apelación.
- Describe el proceso creativo en "Acerca de".

## 4. "Hecho para niños" y COPPA

- **Factores que evalúa YouTube:** tema, audiencia prevista según metadatos, personajes animados o juguetes que atraen a niños, canciones o juegos simples. Tener algunos no lo vuelve automáticamente infantil.
- **Audiencia mixta:** si los niños son una de las audiencias objetivo, cuenta como hecho para niños.
- **Ejemplos oficiales de audiencia general:** "video de gaming con humor adulto" y animación que atrae a todos.
- **Consecuencias de quedar marcado:** sin anuncios personalizados, comentarios, campana de notificaciones, membresías, Super Chat ni Super Stickers, tarjetas, pantallas finales, guardar en listas ni miniplayer. A nivel de canal también se pierden las publicaciones.
- **RPM:** que baje es consecuencia esperable de perder anuncios personalizados, pero no encontré una cifra oficial.
- **Si YouTube anula tu ajuste:** puede marcar el video como "Set to Made for Kids" por error o abuso; hay una sola apelación por video.
- **Cómo mantener audiencia general de forma legítima:**
  - Temas, conflictos y humor para adolescentes y adultos jóvenes (drama escolar, misterio, suspenso, relaciones).
  - Lenguaje y metadatos sin términos como "kids" o "para niños".
  - Sin canciones infantiles ni estética preescolar.
  - Ajuste del canal en "No, no es hecho para niños".
  - No lo tomes como asesoría legal: la FTC puede discrepar de YouTube y la responsabilidad es del creador.

Fuentes:
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9528076
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9527654

## 5. Propiedad intelectual y programas de Roblox

Todo este punto viene de fragmentos de búsqueda, no de lectura directa.

- **Videos monetizados:** un mensaje del personal de Roblox en el DevForum (2022) dice que las pautas no restringen crear videos con avatares R6 o R15 y que puedes seguir monetizando ese contenido, por ejemplo con anuncios de YouTube. El uso comercial fuera de eso (productos físicos, mercancía) requiere licencia o aprobación.
- **Logo y nombre:** el logo y el "Tilt" no se permiten en materiales creativos, salvo dentro de la insignia oficial. Si el canal usa "Roblox" o "Blox" en el nombre, debe decir que no está afiliado a Roblox. Recomiendo no poner "Roblox" en el nombre del canal ni el logo en las miniaturas.
- **Assets de terceros:** modelos, UGC y música del marketplace tienen sus propias licencias. La música con licencia dentro de Roblox no necesariamente cubre YouTube (no verificado).
- **Video Stars:** los requisitos aparecen de forma contradictoria. Para formato corto, 100.000 seguidores y 50.000 vistas promedio por video en 6 meses; para directos, 10.000 seguidores y 300 espectadores concurrentes. Idiomas: inglés, español, portugués, alemán. Cumplir no garantiza el ingreso. No confirmé si acepta solicitudes hoy.
- **Star Codes y Creator Affiliate:** según fuentes secundarias y la documentación, ambos fueron reemplazados por Creator Rewards el 24 de julio de 2025, con retiro de los Star Codes hacia el 24 de octubre de 2025. La página de ayuda de Video Stars aún los menciona.
- **Creator Rewards:** paga 35 % de los primeros 100 USD de compras de un usuario nuevo o reactivado durante 60 días, atribuido por enlaces para compartir. Exige cuenta verificada con identificación y DevEx, y la experiencia debe mantener 100 o más usuarios activos diarios. Está orientado a quien tiene una experiencia; no confirmé que sirva a un creador de video sin juego propio.

## 6. Otras fuentes de ingreso

- **Compilaciones largas:** es la palanca más fuerte, porque el RPM de largos en gaming es unas 10 veces el de Shorts y suman horas para la ruta de 8.000. Riesgo: una compilación que solo pega Shorts ya publicados puede verse como repetitiva; agrega escenas puente o material nuevo. AIR también observa que canales con muchos Shorts muestran menor RPM en sus largos (correlación, no causalidad).
- **Membresías y Super Thanks:** disponibles desde el nivel de 500 suscriptores, en Colombia. No aplican si el contenido queda como hecho para niños.
- **Patrocinios de juegos de Roblox:** existen, pero los datos son de marketplaces y blogs. Rangos citados: 150 a 600 USD por integración para canales de 50.000 a 150.000 seguidores, 500 a 2.500 USD para 200.000 a 500.000, y 30 a 50 USD por un Short en un perfil de CollabPals. No hallé evidencia específica de pagos a canales de historias. Todo patrocinio debe marcarse como promoción pagada en YouTube.
- **TikTok Creator Rewards:** Colombia no aparece como elegible en las fuentes de 2026 (en LATAM, solo Brasil y México de forma consistente). TikTok no publica una lista definitiva; verifícalo en la app. Sirve para distribución, no para ingreso directo.
- **Facebook e Instagram:** una guía de octubre de 2026 que cita el centro de ayuda de Meta dice que Colombia está en la lista de Facebook Content Monetization, pero el acceso es por invitación. No verifiqué la fuente primaria ni encontré un programa de pago por vistas de Reels de Instagram.
- **Snapchat:** el programa unificado es por invitación (unos 50.000 seguidores, 25 publicaciones al mes, videos de más de 1 minuto). Las listas de países se contradicen sobre Colombia; no verificado.

## 7. Estrategia multilenguaje

- **Doblaje automático:** se abrió a todos los creadores en febrero de 2026, con 27 idiomas. De inglés a español está soportado, con "habla expresiva". Puedes activar "Publicar manualmente" para revisar cada doblaje. El video queda etiquetado como "auto-dubbed".
- **Pistas manuales:** puedes subir tu propia pista en español, lo que para un canal con voz de IA da mejor calidad que el doblaje automático.
- **Shorts:** no pude confirmar que el doblaje automático funcione en Shorts; la página oficial no lo dice.
- **¿Canal separado en español?** Mi recomendación (opinión, no dato):
  - Empieza con un solo canal en inglés. El RPM de EE. UU. es entre 5 y 10 veces el de LATAM.
  - Dividir vistas entre dos canales complica llegar a los 20 millones y sostener los 10 millones cada 90 días.
  - Un segundo canal con las mismas historias y otra voz se parece al patrón de red de clones que la política castiga.
  - Agrega pista en español si la función está disponible para tus Shorts. Un canal aparte solo se justifica más adelante con adaptación real: guion localizado y miniaturas y títulos propios.

Fuentes:
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15569972
- https://metricool.com/youtube-multi-language-audio/
- https://blog.google/intl/en-in/products/platforms/unlocking-a-global-audience-with-auto-dubbing/

## Cronograma realista desde cero (estimación mía, no dato)

- **Mes 0 a 1:** define universo y personajes, monta el flujo en Studio, publica 3 a 5 Shorts por semana, configura la audiencia como no infantil y abre AdSense con el W-8BEN cuando se habilite.
- **Mes 1 a 4:** fase de prueba. La mayoría de canales nuevos no supera unos pocos cientos de miles de vistas al mes. Meta intermedia: 500 suscriptores y 3 millones de vistas en 90 días para el nivel de fans.
- **Antes del 1 de febrero de 2027:** solo si un video se vuelve viral y sumas 10 millones en 90 días alcanzarías a entrar con el umbral viejo. Es improbable; no planees con eso.
- **Mes 4 a 12:** escenario base para un canal que sí encuentra formato: 20 millones de vistas en 90 días (unos 6,7 millones al mes) entre los meses 6 y 12. Muchos canales nunca llegan. En paralelo, compilaciones largas mensuales hacia las 8.000 horas.
- **Tras la admisión:** revisión de canal bajo la política de contenido no auténtico; un rechazo suele implicar esperar 30 días para volver a solicitar (plazo habitual, no verificado en esta sesión).
- **Ingreso esperable al entrar:** con 7 a 10 millones de vistas mensuales de Shorts, unos 700 a 3.000 USD brutos al mes con audiencia de EE. UU., menos cerca de 30 % de retención.

## Riesgos, de mayor a menor

1. **Umbral nuevo y piso de Shorts:** 20 millones para entrar y 10 millones cada 90 días para cobrar. Un bajón de vistas pausa el ingreso.
2. **Rechazo o desmonetización por contenido no auténtico:** el perfil faceless, con voz y guion de IA y alta frecuencia, es el más vigilado; hay falsos positivos documentados en Roblox y las apelaciones son lentas.
3. **Clasificación forzada como hecho para niños:** Roblox con personajes animados es zona gris.
4. **RPM bajo de Shorts más 30 % de retención:** el negocio solo cierra con volumen alto o con largos y patrocinios.
5. **Errores de moderación automática sobre contenido de Roblox** (precedente de diciembre de 2025).
6. **Dependencia de Roblox:** cambios en sus pautas de marca o en su relación con creadores; la monetización de videos se apoya en un mensaje de foro de 2022, no en una licencia explícita que yo haya podido leer.
7. **Música y assets de terceros:** reclamos de derechos, y la deducción del fondo si usas música.
8. **Plataformas alternas sin pago directo en Colombia:** TikTok no elegible; Meta y Snapchat por invitación.
9. **Cambios regulatorios:** los criterios de los nuevos incentivos de YouTube aún no existen.
